metadata.name: Consolidated Edison (CECONY)
metadata.dollar_basis: Nominal dollars. Cumulative figures undiscounted unless labelled npv3_2026 (NPV at 3%, 2026 dollars). Bills are the average residential bill, $/month.
metadata.flows_note: Customer savings split residential / business by the residential share of sales (EIA-861, 2024).
metadata.share_sweep_note: Each scenario and pace re-run at utility_share 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 with every other input fixed (default 0.30). Value creation is held constant across shares: the share moves value between customers and the utility; it does not change what flexibility delivers.
metadata.objective_sweep_note: Each scenario and pace re-run with an additional savings objective of 0 / 2.5 / 5 / 10% of its base (default 0%, base dist_revenue_requirement, net of 20% cost to achieve), every other input fixed. The objective is additional to the other layers by assumption.
metadata.objective_sweep_run_note: Each objective_sweep level carries its full chart data under run (yearly, waterfall_usd_month, value_flows_m), built exactly as the top-level run block.
metadata.earnings_note: earnings_total_m = equity return on rate base + shared savings earnings; earnings_per_rate_base = earnings_total_m / rate base (wires + program regulatory asset).
metadata.advance_note: advance: each scenario with the customer dividend advance on (default off in the model), at its enabled defaults: level bill credit for advance_credit_years from 2027 sized at 0.5 x the PV (at the financing rate) of the Cautious scenario recoverable savings, securitized at 4%, recovered through a rider withholding a share of each year total customer saving vs BAU (bill_savings), on a schedule that tracks credits actually paid; true-up pauses credits when behind schedule; recoveries capped so customers net saving is never negative. advance_stress: sized on Central, realized Cautious. worst_year_vs_bau = the largest shared-savings minus BAU average residential bill.
metadata.fast_start_note: fast_start: each scenario and pace with mechanism.fast_start on (first savings year 2027; near-term ramps at their defaults, i.e. none): yearly, waterfall_usd_month, value_flows_m and headline. advance_fast_start: the advance at its enabled defaults with fast start on; advance_fast_start_stress: the same, sized on Central and realized Cautious.
metadata.allocation_sweep_note: allocation_sweep: each scenario and pace with the pool's customer share (the wires and program revenue-requirement reduction net of shared savings earnings, recovered through delivery rates) split between residential and non-residential customers by_sales (default: residential share of sales, EIA-861), per_customer (equal per customer: residential share of EIA-861 2024 customer counts) or custom (residential share 0.5). Capacity, transmission, losses, wholesale and efficiency energy savings follow load through existing rates and stay split by sales. Totals are the same under every option; by_sales equals the run block. Residential bills move by the reallocated amount per residential customer; non-residential savings per customer use EIA-861 2024 counts, held constant.
metadata.lookback_note: lookback: the starting point 2021-2026 from utilities/<utility>_lookback.json (engine/lookback.py; every figure with source, as_of and status). bill_comparison: 2021 (EIA-861 average revenue per kWh at the benchmark usage where line items were not located) against the 2026 starting bill by category. rr_bridge: distribution revenue requirement on a FERC Form 1 functional basis 2021 -> 2025, then the approved 2026 rate-case step ($M nominal). supply_side: influenced, not controlled, by the distribution utility.
metadata.tornado_note: Tornado at Central (every input at central; low and high one at a time), per pace; change in the average residential monthly saving vs Central.

lookback.note: Look-back module (engine/lookback.py): the starting point 2021-2026. Every figure carries a source, an as_of date and a status (sourced / derived / _VERIFY / setting). The forward model does not read this file. Dollar figures are nominal and undiscounted.

bill_comparison.basis_2021: EIA-861 2021 average revenue per kWh at the benchmark usage (no 2021 line-item tariff archive was located; per the fallback rule, marked derived)
bill_comparison.basis_2026: utilities/ConEd.json starting_bill (line by line, statuses there), by category via engine.layers.starting_lines() with the capacity carve-out and starting adjustments

scope.note: New York delivery rates recover distribution and the utility's transmission, so the functional scope is distribution + transmission (the forward model's delivery revenue requirement).

2021.source: CECONY electric is a single New York jurisdiction

2025.source: CECONY electric is a single New York jurisdiction

rr_bridge.note: Revenue requirement on a Form 1 functional basis for 2021 and 2025 (return on functional rate base at the allowed after-tax WACC, depreciation, O&M, taxes other than income, income taxes; general, intangible and A&G costs allocated to the scope by plant or O&M share; jurisdictional share applied), then the approved 2026 rate-case step. Computed in engine/lookback.py with the forward model's revenue-requirement structure.

step_2026.source: NY DPS, Consolidated Edison Electric Rate Case Summary (Case 25-E-0072, Jan 2026): RY1 (2026) electric revenue increase $234 million

supply_side.influence: Influenced, not controlled, by the distribution utility: set by wholesale markets (PJM / NYISO auctions), FERC formula rates or fuel markets; the utility affects them only through its load, procurement and the resources it connects.
